newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba shows jump in HIV positives.
newsitem.headline: Cuba shows jump in HIV positives.

text.p: Cuba experienced a substantial increase in the number of AIDS cases in 1996 due primarily to a growth of foreign tourism and an increase in prostitution, health officials said.
The Juventud Rebelde newspaper on Sunday said since AIDS testing began in 1985, government-run hospitals and clinics have detected 1,609 HIV positive cases.
In 1995 the total was reported at 1,196 meaning that 413 new cases were detected in 1996. This compared with only 97 new cases reported during 1995.
AIDS among the island's 11 million inhabitants remained relatively low due to a massive testing programme and a public health infrastructure that provides universal, free medical treatment.
Cuba was a pioneer in the use of interferon on HIV positive persons. Cuba produces its own interferon, which prolongs the life expectancy of patients, and also reagents for AIDS' testing.

There are special sanitariums for AIDS patients in most of Cuba's 12 provinces. Cuban adults who test HIV positive are required to enter the sanitariums in a policy reminiscent of the way tuberculosis patients were treated in the United States earlier in the century.

Officials said the isolation of patients in sanitariums has been somewhat relaxed over past years by introducing greater flexibility in allowing persons who are considered reliable to live at home or make prolonged visits.
